question: A 22-year-old woman took 15 g of paracetamol 8 hours ago. She is currently asymptomatic with normal vitals. Her 8-hour serum paracetamol level plots ABOVE the treatment line on the Rumack-Matthew nomogram. What is the CORRECT next step?

answers.text: Observe for 24 hours; initiate N-acetylcysteine (NAC) only if LFTs rise

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Waiting for LFT rise is too late — the silent phase of paracetamol toxicity means hepatocellular injury is already occurring before LFTs become abnormal. NAC must be started immediately based on the nomogram.

Correct. When the paracetamol level at 4–24 hours post-ingestion plots on or above the treatment line (150 μg/mL at 4h), IV NAC must be started immediately. NAC is the specific antidote — it replenishes hepatic glutathione, conjugating the toxic NAPQI metabolite.

answers.text: Administer activated charcoal and discharge if asymptomatic at 12 hours

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: At 8 hours post-ingestion, activated charcoal provides little benefit (absorption nearly complete). The asymptomatic state in the first 24 hours is MISLEADING — hepatotoxicity peaks at 72–96 hours.
Haemodialysis is NOT the treatment for paracetamol overdose. NAC is the specific antidote. Dialysis may be considered for established fulminant hepatic failure but is not the primary intervention.

overallFeedback.feedback: The Rumack-Matthew nomogram is the cornerstone of paracetamol overdose management. A level on or above the treatment line at any time between 4–24 hours mandates immediate IV NAC regardless of symptoms.

Exactly right. The Rumack-Matthew nomogram at ≥4 hours post-ingestion guides NAC initiation. An asymptomatic patient with a level above the treatment line MUST receive IV NAC immediately — do not wait for symptoms.
